podcast.body: A mega-blockbuster hit officially credited to Mark Ronson featuring Bruno Mars, who was acknowledged as the song's "animating force." The song began with Mars's improvisation in an LA studio, involved extensive sessions across studios in six cities (Memphis, New York, London, Vancouver, etc.), featured three different horn sections (including Mars's band The Hooligans and Mark Ronson collaborators The Dap-Kings), required over 100 takes, and famously had Philip Lawrence singing the bass line due to recording difficulties. Released in November 2014, critics lauded its recreation of turn-of-the-80s electro-funk and R&B, noting numerous references to artists like James Brown, The Sequence, Kool & The Gang, George Kranz, Rick James, George Clinton, Zapp (featuring Roger Troutman), and The Gap Band, who successfully sued for a belated songwriting credit due to similarities with their 1979 hit "Oops Up Side Your Head." It spent 14 weeks at number one on the Hot 100 in early 2015, becoming the second longest run in chart history at the time, and earned the Grammy for Record of the Year. "Uptown Funk was credited officially to Mark Ronson, the British born American-raised producer who had already won Grammys for Helming Hits by Amy Winehouse and Adele."

podcast.body: This song, co-written with Mark Ronson, became the target of multiple plagiarism lawsuits following the "Blurred Lines" precedent. Various groups, including The Gap Band, The Sequence, Kalash, Zap, and Serbian singer Victoria, accused them of infringement. As a result, the songwriting credits and royalties for "Uptown Funk" are now split among Mark Ronson, Bruno Mars, and ten other individuals who had no direct involvement in the specific recording. "Some of the first people to be hit with such a lawsuit were Bruno Mars and Mark Ronson for the song Uptown Funk."
